A.justification: Strong SQL-injection section with a group_by whitelist and both ORM and parameterized-raw fixes, and decent object-level permission classes. But it is truncated early (never reaches secrets or the staff/mass-assignment serializer issue), and the permission/serializer code has real inconsistencies: 'owner' is both read_only and mapped via a write_only owner_id field, and IsAdminOrReadOnly denies all non-safe object access regardless of role.

B.justification: Cleanest and most idiomatic response: correct CWE-89 with ORM + enum whitelist, strong object-level fix centered on get_queryset() scoping (the key multi-tenant defense), and solid env-var/dotenv secrets management. Minor PUT permission logic is a touch loose, and it is truncated before an explicit serializer allowlisting/mass-assignment issue, so it misses the fourth required fix.

C.justification: Well-structured with named-parameter SQL, get_queryset tenant scoping, and django-environ secrets. However, CombinedObjectPermissions has a real authorization bug: multiple-inheritance MRO means IsTenantMember.has_object_permission shadows IsOwnerOrReadOnly, so within-tenant writes are not owner-restricted. Also truncates before the serializer-allowlisting issue and makes both dates mandatory, changing behavior.

D.justification: Issue 1 is correct and clean (named placeholders + status whitelist + ORM alternative), but the response is cut off after SQL injection, covering only one of the four required vulnerabilities and none of the other mandated fixes (object authorization, secrets, serializer allowlisting).

E.justification: Solid across SQL injection (column whitelist + parameterized values), object-level authorization (permission classes, queryset scoping, and CurrentTenantMiddleware), and secrets management. A few minor nits (mysql.connector in the vulnerable example feels off for Django; logging touches request.user.pk) and it truncates before the serializer allowlisting/mass-assignment issue, but no major correctness or security flaw is present.

raw_result.pairwise_analysis: B ranks first because it is the most correct and idiomatic, emphasizing queryset-scoped tenant isolation and clean env-var secrets without introducing bugs. E and C both cover three issues, but E edges out C because C's CombinedObjectPermissions inheritance bug silently drops the owner check on writes, whereas E keeps tenant scoping and ownership checks coherent. A and D trail because they are truncated earliest — A also contains internal serializer/permission inconsistencies, and D covers only the SQL-injection issue, leaving the other three required fixes unaddressed.
